chapter: Ellington, the South, bebop and radio
title: Returning South with Claude Hopkins
summary: He went South again with Claude Hopkins without incident like that, enjoyed the band, and says Fred Norman did most of the writing.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: But I did go down again. I did go down... I didn't go down... I was a glutton for punishment. I went down with Claude Hopkins. We had no incidents like that, quite like that.
But there was still the whole atmosphere...
It was still there. There was a little incident when Jabbo was in the band, and somebody wanted him to drink up a lot of whiskey or something. I forget.
Yeah, Jabbo could tell you about that if you ever had an interview with him. He could tell you about that scene.
Yeah, I guess if you didn't have to go down there, there was no good reason for it.
I was with a band, and what are you going to do? And I liked playing with Claude. It was a good band.
That was sort of a... I don't know if you'd say soft, but sort of like a pretty band. Right?
Did Fred Norman do most of the writing?
